md_south_bank_tick_area.blurb: A small bouldering zone on the south side of Northwest Branch, in the creek corridor. It holds about fourteen problems from V0 up to V5, and roughly half of them sit at V4 or V5, so there is something for a mixed group but a bit more for strong boulderers. The centrepiece is a low, elongated block with a prow-like corner that is easy to pad and offers room for variations, often marked with graffiti. Getting here means crossing the creek, and the current can run fast, so judge the water before you commit. Bring pads and a spotter.

md_howling_wall.blurb: A trad-only cliff in the Cumberland Narrows, the stretch of western Maryland cliffs also known as Lover's Leap. The wall carries thirteen routes from 5.3 to 5.10, with most falling between 5.7 and 5.9, and includes at least one two-pitch line. It breaks into a small side section, where the ground at the base is cramped, and a bigger main wall that is the better draw. Rock here can be loose, so belayers should wear helmets and leaders should test holds before trusting them. Expect a traditional rack and a modest crowd.

md_funland.blurb: A friendly trad sector of the Cumberland Narrows (Lover's Leap) cliffs in western Maryland, set partway up the hillside above town. Thirteen routes cover 5.3 to 5.9, almost all of them placed protection climbs plus one top-rope variation, and most sit at moderate grades. That spread makes it a sensible place to practise leading on gear. Horizontal striations in the rock give a good supply of cracks and edges. The approach is a short uphill hike of around fifteen minutes on a small path through the trees.

md_hog_rock.parking_note: Use the fourth parking lot counted out from the visitor center along the park road, then continue on foot along the trail.
md_hog_rock.blurb: A bouldering zone in Catoctin Mountain Park, in the hills of northern Maryland. Thirteen problems run from very easy to a standout V10, with the bulk in the V3 to V6 range. The area centres on one main boulder with traverses, a centre line and some harder lines, while more blocks and overhung faces lie along the approach trail and down the slope, some of them reached by bushwhacking. Expect woods rather than a clean landing zone, so bring pads and a spotter, and a flat half-mile walk gets you there from the lot.

md_gorsuch_switch.blurb: A lone boulder in Patapsco Valley State Park, further down river than the park's main climbing zones and reached from its own separate parking point. It offers a compact mix of thirteen climbs: seven boulder problems, mostly V0 to V2 with a couple of hard V5s, and six top-rope lines from easy up to about 5.7. Handy for a short session or for introducing newer climbers to the rope side, but it is a one-boulder stop rather than a destination.
